subject: OptiVis modular pricing + vendor swap checklist
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@optivis.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@optivis.com>, procurement@optivis.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: vendor replacement economics and modular packaging

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to put the ask in writing so we can compare apples-to-apples with our incumbent. Topline: OptiVis is evaluating a mid‑enterprise replacement during Q3 and we need a compact pricing and packaging proposal that maps to our current runtime mix.

Key asks: 
- A modular price table (in tokens or endpoint-hours) we can slot into our model mix.
- A one-page runbook for migration cost (eg. credits, egress assumptions, pilot pricing).
- Any enterprise-level concessions you’d need to make for a 12–18 month commitment.

Attached is our RFP/usage snapshot (OptiVis_RFP_v3.pdf). Can you send a concise comparison and a priced modular bundle by end of week? We’ve also asked for any explicit parity or credits you’d offer to match existing committed economics.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
OptiVis

Attachments: OptiVis_RFP_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena@optivis.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: vendor replacement economics and modular packaging

Elena —

Thanks for sharing the RFP. I ran a quick scan with Marissa and Connor to scope a focused deliverable (price table + migration checklist + optional credit buckets). We’ll send a modular quote and a short migration playbook that maps to the three usage segments you highlighted.

To keep this tight and useful, two tidbits we need from you: 
1) % of traffic that needs latency SLOs (<200ms) vs batch processing (can accept 2–10s).
2) Expected monthly token/embedding volumes by model class for the first 6 months (or the current month if you only have that).

Assume we’ll propose: 
- Base modular bundles (API generation, embeddings, private routing) priced per token/hour;
- A 90‑day pilot credit and a migration credit tied to paid MRR if you convert;
- Optional Dedicated node uplift for strict latency workloads.

We’ll turn around an initial matrix by Thu EOD. If you’re open to a quick 25‑minute call tomorrow we can resolve the latency split and we’ll remove guesswork from the quote. 

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-modular-pricing-quote.xlsx (placeholder - will be delivered Thu)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: pricing guardrails for OptiVis counteroffer

Rishi — quick internal note before we send the public quote:

I reviewed the incumbent numbers in their RFP and pulled prior swap playbook figures. Recommend we offer two scenarios:

A) Standard swap: 15% on list + $60k onboarding credit (applied as one-time) for a 12‑month commit; includes: 30% pilot credit (applied over 3 months), basic onboarding support.
B) Aggressive parity: 22% discount on the runtime unit + $120k spread upgrade credit + 2 months free for dedicated nodes for a 12‑18 month committed ARR above $1.2M.

Constraints: finance needs to sign off on >20% list discount — route to Markus if client asks to go deeper. Also flag any ask for multi‑year guaranteed prepay to Legal for SOW carveouts.

Put Connor on technical line items (KV cache, runtime compatibility, sequence-length behavior). I’ll own commercial framing and the migration credit buckets.

Marissa
VP Sales Ops

[Internal tagging: budget-approval, swap-playbook]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena@optivis.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, procurement@optivis.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood modular quote + migration checklist (first pass)

Elena / Paul —

Thanks for the RFP. Attached is a concise package that aims to make vendor comparison straightforward:

Highlights (high level):
- Three modular bundles: Core (api gen + embeddings), Performance (Core + reserved dedicated pool for <200ms SLO), and Enterprise (Performance + expanded retention/audit logging).
- Pilot: 3‑month pilot with 30% credit (applied to token usage), plus a $60k migration credit if you convert to a 12‑month committed plan.
- Parity option: if you can share incumbent committed ARR and term, we’ll evaluate an up to 22% list discount for a 12–18 month ARR commitment (requires finance approval).

Attached: redwood-modular-pricing-quote.xlsx (pricing matrix), SOW-draft-OptiVis.docx (sample SOW).

Quick asks to finalize: 
- Confirm latency split (SLO vs batch) so Connor can size the dedicated uplift.
- Confirm expected first–month token/embedding volumes (or a 3‑month rolling average).

If helpful, we can lock a brief call Fri 10:00am PT to walk the matrix and call out migration blockers. If not, reply with the two datapoints and we’ll produce the final redline-ready offer.

Thanks —
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0104

Attachments: redwood-modular-pricing-quote.xlsx, SOW-draft-OptiVis.docx

From: Paul Chen <paul.chen@optivis.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood modular quote + migration checklist (first pass)

Rishi / Marissa / Connor —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear matrix. A few quick datapoints to unblock: 
- Latency split: ~18% low-latency (<200ms) production traffic, 62% interactive non‑SLO (0.5–2s ok), 20% batch/async.
- Estimated month 1 volume: 1.2B tokens gen, 420M embedding tokens.

We’re encouraged by the pilot + $60k migration credit. Procurement would like to see an explicit comparison row that normalizes: effective unit price (post-credit) and effective TCV over 12 months at our profile. Can you add a line in the matrix that shows "effective per-token after credits" and a TCV row? Also, if we provide incumbent committed ARR, what’s your exact ask for finance sign-off (i.e., what docs or board-level approvals are needed to get to the 22% parity)?

If you can update the matrix by EOD Mon we’ll have internal scoring completed and can move to redlines.

Thanks,
Paul Chen
Procurement Manager, OptiVis
